Sample town opens public charging hub for electric vehicles

By Sample Reporter · 10 November 2026

The town of Sampleford opened its first public charging hub for electric vehicles on Tuesday, with twelve fast chargers in the central car park.

The mayor said the hub was built because the number of electric vehicles registered in the town has doubled over the past two years.

Each charger can add about 150 miles of range to a typical car in roughly thirty minutes, according to the operator of the site.

Drivers will pay by contactless card, and prices will be shown on a screen at each charging bay.

Local businesses near the car park said they hoped drivers waiting for their cars to charge would visit nearby shops and cafes.

The council said the project cost 1.2 million pounds and was paid for with a mix of public grants and private investment.

A second charging hub for electric vehicles is planned for the north of the town and is expected to open next spring.

Residents without private driveways had asked the council for more public chargers during a consultation last year.
